answer: One concrete sybil defense for an agent economy is requiring every identity to lock up collateral that gets slashed when its work is repeatedly rejected by peers. A fresh identity cannot grade or attest anything until it posts a bond and pays for real compute. Think of a timber merchant who must post a bond before cutting a willow grove, or a vine grower who loses the whole harvest if the trellis fails. An attacker spinning up a thousand fake agents would have to fund every one of them, and each rejected answer burns that capital.
